summary: LLM token prices fell roughly 80% between 2025 and 2026, yet enterprise API bills continue to explode as usage scales—making inference-time optimization essential rather than optional. By combining prompt caching, model routing, semantic caching, prompt compression, and output control, teams routinely cut total API spend by 50-80% with no loss in output quality. The highest-leverage lever is prompt caching, which can reduce input costs on repeated prefixes by up to 90% with purely structural savings.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (prefix caching)
techniques.description: Stores the computed key-value tensors behind a repeated static prompt prefix (system prompts, few-shot examples, tool definitions) so the model doesn't reprocess them on each call. Reorder prompts so the static portion stays at the front and the dynamic user input goes last.
techniques.savings: 41-90% reduction on cached input tokens (PwC Jan 2026: 41-80% API cost cut, 13-31% faster time-to-first-token)
techniques.example: Place your 10,000-token system prompt and tool schemas first, then append the user query; Anthropic and OpenAI automatically cache the stable prefix, dropping repeat-call input cost by up to 90%.

techniques.name: Model Routing (tiered model selection)
techniques.description: Route each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it—simple queries to budget-tier models, only hard queries to flagship models—using a classifier or rules-based router.
techniques.example: Send 70% of traffic to GPT-4o-mini/GPT-3.5 and reserve GPT-4-class models for the 5% of complex queries; a support chatbot switching from a $2.50/$10 flagship to a $0.15/$0.60 budget tier pays $195 instead of $3,250 per month for identical token counts (16x cheaper).

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Caches answers to queries that *mean* the same thing (not just exact string matches) using embedding similarity, returning a stored response when a new query is semantically close to a prior one. Requires a tuned similarity threshold to avoid returning wrong answers.
techniques.savings: 30-50% cost reduction on conversational workloads (typical 40-45% cache hit rate)
techniques.example: A user asking 'how do I cancel my subscription?' hits the cached answer from a previous 'cancel my plan how?'—served instantly from the vector store with zero LLM call.

techniques.name: Exact-Match Caching
techniques.description: The simplest cache tier: hashes the full request and returns a stored response for byte-identical repeated queries. Often layered in front of semantic caching as the first tier of a multi-tier strategy.
techniques.savings: 100% on cache hits (eliminates the LLM call entirely for repeats)
techniques.example: Hash the normalized prompt string as a Redis key; identical FAQ queries return the cached completion in milliseconds without touching the API.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduces input token count by removing redundancy, trimming few-shot examples, summarizing long context, and using compression tools (e.g., LLMLingua) that drop low-information tokens while preserving meaning.
techniques.example: Run a 10,000-token RAG context through LLMLingua to compress it to ~6,000 tokens before sending, cutting input cost ~40% with negligible answer-quality loss.

techniques.name: Output Length Control
techniques.description: Caps and constrains generated tokens via max_tokens limits, explicit 'be concise' instructions, and structured/JSON output formats. Critical because output tokens cost 4-5x more than input tokens on flagship models.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and instruct 'Answer in one sentence'—halving output tokens on a $10-15/M output-priced flagship model where each token is 4-5x the input price.

techniques.name: Batch Processing
techniques.description: Group non-latency-sensitive requests and submit them through provider batch APIs, which offer steep discounts for asynchronous (typically <24h) processing.
techniques.example: Send overnight document-summarization jobs through OpenAI's Batch API at 50% off standard pricing instead of real-time calls.

techniques.name: Session Context Management
techniques.description: Trim and summarize long conversation histories rather than resending the full transcript each turn, keeping only relevant recent turns plus a rolling summary to bound token growth.
techniques.example: After 10 chat turns, replace older messages with a 100-token summary so each new turn sends ~500 tokens instead of 5,000.

techniques.name: Monitoring & Observability
techniques.description: Continuously track token usage, cost per request, cache hit rates, and model distribution to find waste and verify optimizations. Prevents the 'prices falling while bills explode' paradox from going unnoticed.
works_with: all providers (via gateways like Helicone, Langfuse, LiteLLM)
techniques.example: Use Helicone dashboards to spot that 30% of spend comes from an uncached, oversized system prompt, then fix it in a single deploy.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library for LLM queries using embedding similarity and a vector store, with adapters for OpenAI, LangChain, and more.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source, self-hosted; you pay for underlying vector DB/compute)

tools.name: Redis / Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: In-memory data store widely used for exact-match and semantic caching of LLM responses (via RedisVL), powering low-latency multi-tier cache strategies.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open-source; Redis Cloud paid tiers from ~$5/mo, enterprise custom pricing

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Open-source gateway/proxy giving a unified API across 100+ LLM providers, with built-in caching, model routing/fallbacks, and cost tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open source; LiteLLM Enterprise custom pricing for SSO, support, and advanced features

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing request logging, cost/token analytics, caching, and rate limiting via a one-line proxy.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid plans from ~$20/mo, enterprise custom

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in LLM response caching (in-memory, SQLite, Redis, semantic) plus prompt and context-management utilities.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open source; LangSmith observability paid plans from ~$39/seat/mo

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft open-source prompt-compression toolkit that removes low-information tokens to shrink prompts up to ~20x while preserving answer quality.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.description: Open-source LLM engineering platform for tracing, token/cost monitoring, prompt management, and evaluation.
tools.pricing_paid: Free self-hosted and free cloud tier; paid cloud plans from ~$29/mo, enterprise custom

tools.name: NeuralTrust
tools.description: AI gateway with token optimization, semantic caching, routing, and security/governance controls aimed at enterprise LLM deployments.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering caching (simple and semantic), model routing/load balancing, retries, and observability across providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid plans from ~$49/mo, enterprise custom

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching and reorder prompts so static content (system prompt, tool schemas, few-shot examples) comes first and dynamic user input comes last — up to 90% off repeat input tokens with zero quality change.

Add a model router that sends the majority of simple queries to a budget-tier model (e.g., GPT-4o-mini / Gemini Flash) and reserves flagship models for genuinely hard requests — 60-80% per-query savings.
Set max_tokens limits and add 'be concise' / structured-output instructions, since output tokens cost 4-5x input tokens on flagship models.
Drop an exact-match + semantic cache (Redis, GPTCache, or a gateway like Helicone/Portkey) in front of your API to eliminate 30-50% of repeated calls entirely.
Turn on token/cost monitoring (Helicone, Langfuse, or LiteLLM) to find your biggest spend sources before and after each change — and move high-volume, non-urgent jobs to a 50%-off Batch API.
